group: q|how long does the top 1% of people live to

result.why: The question asks for the age at death reached only by the longest-lived 1% of people (p99 of the age-at-death distribution, both sexes, world by default). This is not the catalogue metric life_expectancy_at_birth, which is a mean. If it ships, it needs a new metric, roughly id age_at_death, unit years, direction high, format years_1dp, defined as age at death under a current period life table. I could not get a both-sexes value from a source I was able to read. (1) CDC/NCHS, United States Life Tables, 2022 (NVSR Vol. 74 No. 2, 8 April 2025; https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/Health_Statistics/NCHS/Publications/NVSR/74-02/). I read the published l(x) column, survivors out of 100,000 births, period table, for each sex. Males: l(79)=50,707, l(80)=48,007; l(92)=11,200, l(93)=8,862; l(99)=1,184, l(100 and older)=753. So the male median falls between ages 79 and 80, p90 between 92 and 93, and p99 between 99 and 100. Females: l(84)=50,272, l(85)=46,871; l(95)=11,099, l(96)=8,570; l(100 and older)=2,242. So the female median falls between 84 and 85, p90 between 95 and 96, and p99 above 100. The table closes with an open 100+ interval, so the female p99 and probably the both-sexes p99 lie above 100 and cannot be read from it. 2.2% of females and 0.75% of males survive to 100. The both-sexes Table 1 (Table01.xlsx) downloaded only as a compressed binary that I could not parse. (2) The SSA period life tables (ssa.gov/oact/STATS/table4c6.html and HistEst/PerLifeTables/2022) run to age 119 and would give the both-sexes p99 directly, but every request returned HTTP 403. (3) Verguet, Niwa and Bolongaita, 'Top and bottom longevity of nations', European Journal of Public Health 2023 (PMC10132764), publishes the 99th percentile of age at death for 18 OECD countries from 1900 to 2020 using Human Mortality Database data. The full text was behind a browser check, so I could not read the values. (4) For the world, UN WPP 2024 single-age life tables would be the right source, but I found no readable copy. Next run: read SSA period table 4c6 (ages 0 to 119, by sex), the both-sexes table in NVSR 74-02, the Verguet et al. tables, or UN WPP 2024 world life tables. Pick one population (US or world, both sexes) and keep male-only or female-only figures out of a both-sexes grid.
